issues.title: design(hiring): W3 -- revisit the candidate pool cap (MAX_CANDIDATES=6); stale once networking changes, and cap-hits are partly silent
issues.body:
Pip ruling (2026-07-26): the candidate pool cap needs revisiting in W3 if not before -- the cap may be stale as the way networking/sourcing works changes.

## Current state: MAX_CANDIDATES = 6, and it bites in several places

- `game_state.gd:104` -- `const MAX_CANDIDATES: int = 6`, hardcoded (NOT Balance-sourced, unlike most hiring tunables).
- `game_state.gd:597 add_candidate` -- **silently drops** the candidate when the pool is full. No log, no event.
- `hiring_pipeline.gd:186 _add_sourced_candidate` -- returns false at cap. The connections path emits a `connection_pool_full` event (hiring_pipeline.gd:719), but the ADVERTISE path just skips the `advertise_hit` event: **paid campaign candidates are silently discarded at cap**. This is the same failure mode that got the old free per-turn refill removed (see the NOTE at the top of turn_manager.gd) -- sourcing spend competing with a tiny fixed pool.
- `turn_manager.gd _restore_stranded_hires` (PR #960) -- a stranded hire returning to a FULL pool "takes another offer" (visible, but still a loss driven by the cap).
- `hiring_panel_controller.gd:120` -- UI header renders `CANDIDATE POOL (n/6)`.

## Questions for W3

- Is a fixed cap even the right shape once networking changes, or should pool size scale with something (reputation, org size, sourcing investment, an upgrade)?
- If a cap stays: what happens at cap must NEVER be silent -- displacement (worst candidate leaves), refusal-with-message, or a queue, but not a silent drop.
- First step regardless of the design ruling: move the constant to Balance (`hiring.pool_cap` or similar) so it is tunable data, not a const.

Related: #830 (hiring statefulness), #833 (people-and-money cohesion spine), #954 (full candidate cards -- a bigger pool changes that UI's scale assumptions).

issues.title: fix(hiring): drain stranded pending_hire_queue back to the pool each turn (#952)
issues.body:
Fixes the verified half of #952.

## Bug

`queue_candidate_hire` (game_manager.gd:251) removes the candidate from `candidate_pool` the moment the hire is queued, but `execute_action` bails on the affordability check (actions.gd:231) BEFORE the `hire_*_researcher` arm calls `_hire_from_pool`. On that path the candidate was stuck in `pending_hire_queue` forever: not in the pool, never employed, invisible -- and the queue round-trips through saves, so the leak persisted.

Trigger in normal play: cash drops between queuing and execution (an earlier action in the same turn's execution order), so the hire fails and the candidate silently vanishes.

## Fix

New `_restore_stranded_hires` step at the end of `_step_execute_queued_actions`: hires only span a single turn's action step, so anyone still queued after it is stranded by definition -- return them to the pool, or narrate the walk-away in the results log if the pool refilled to cap (never a silent vanish). No RNG touched (stream-neutral); also self-heals stranded candidates in existing saves on their next turn.

## Tests

Two guard tests in `test_turn_manager.gd`: failed hire returns the candidate to the pool and employs nobody; full-pool edge drains the queue, respects the cap, and narrates the walk-away.

Fast gate: 801 tests, 0 failures, 85/85 files collected.

issues.title: bug(hiring): queued hire that fails at execution strands the candidate -- vanishes from pool AND queue forever
issues.body:
## Origin (funny)

Filed 2026-07-26 as "28 people ballooning mid-run" from Pip's playtest note "28 visitors, something weird is happening." That turned out to be **28 WEBSITE visitors** (traffic, and good news), not a game bug. The original premise is dead -- but the code archaeology it triggered surfaced a real, verified candidate-leak path, so this issue is repurposed for that.

## The real bug: queued hires can strand candidates (they vanish from the game)

Flow:

1. Player hires a named candidate: `game_manager.gd:251 queue_candidate_hire` appends the Researcher to `state.pending_hire_queue` and **removes them from `candidate_pool` immediately** (double-hire guard).
2. At end-of-turn execution, `actions.gd:231` checks `state.can_afford(execution_costs)` and returns failure **before** the `hire_*_researcher` match arm ever calls `_hire_from_pool`.
3. On that failure path the queued candidate is **never popped from `pending_hire_queue` and never restored to the pool**. Nothing else drains stale queue entries -- the only clears are new-game reset (`game_state.gd:265`) and save-load overwrite (`game_state.gd:1163`, which faithfully round-trips the stranded entry).

Result: if cash drops between queuing and execution (earlier action in the same turn's execution order, an event, payroll), the candidate silently disappears -- not in the pool, not employed, carried forever in a queue no one reads. Player-visible symptom: "I hired someone and they never showed up, and they're gone from the pool."

Secondary path (unverified, lower priority): `actions.gd:679-689` `_hire_from_pool` only dequeues a spec-MATCHING candidate; the normal UI derives the action id from the candidate's own spec so a mismatch should be unreachable today, but the fallthrough silently hires a different pool candidate if it ever happens. Worth an assert.

## Fix sketch

- On the affordability-failure path (and any failure between queue and hire), return the queued candidate to `candidate_pool` (respecting `MAX_CANDIDATES`; if full, at minimum log + drop visibly).
- Or: drain `pending_hire_queue` at end of turn execution -- anyone still queued goes back to the pool with a log line.
- Guard test: queue a hire, force cash below execution cost, end turn, assert candidate is back in the pool and queue is empty.

issues.body:
RESTRUCTURED 2026-07-26 evening (Pip ruling, anniversary-driven: his first GitHub issue was 2025-07-30, and W-4 lands on the eve of the one-year mark): the single Wed 07-29 workshop becomes a THREE-DAY block. **Mon 2026-07-27 = W-3a** -- the ratify block (WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP's 5 questions) + build-gating decisions ONLY (early-game decisions design, #613 effort-economy scheduling, tile-grid addressing ruling, office-view real-estate/camera ruling); ~5 focused hours AROUND Pip's day-job CEO chunks. **Tue 2026-07-28 = BUILD DAY** -- Fable orchestrates the implementation fan-out of Monday's rulings + the in-flight art re-base; Pip mostly ignores it (CEO chunks + drive-by approvals, the proven 27-PR co-orchestration mode). **Wed 2026-07-29 = W-3b/W-4** -- colour architecture circle-back, interior-decorating math + office-fullness, league/content cadence + Fri 07-31 league prep, REVIEW of Tuesday's builds, next-epoch planning. Blow-by-blow schedule: `docs/game-design/RUNSHEET_2026-07-27_to_29.md` (CEO chunks are MOVABLE placeholders; 30-min feed-triage slots daily -- Manifund inbound expected; hard stops, no heroics; Fri 17:30 Rektango anchor). On the release calendar. (Superseded: the earlier single-day "Wed 2026-07-29 0800-1800 AEST" plan.)

Thesis (Pip's ruling): **"crisp parts, brutal decisions"** -- suffer-hardness lives in the DECISIONS, never in the INTERFACE. Claude runs a standing MaRo/Rams simplicity check.

## Agenda (ordered by leverage; from the 2026-07-24 tension audit + deferred rulings)

(Day mapping under the three-day structure: items 1-2 -> Mon W-3a; items 3-4 -> Wed W-3b/W-4.)

1. **Early-game decisions design (the big one).** Offices (choose 1 of 3), non-profit/for-profit DEPTH (the minimal np/fp choice ships Friday as pricing-only; design the real divergence), first-funding modes (each mode gets 3 of 4 finance options), and the scouting actions (read / go-to-meetups / shitpost) -- NONE of which exist yet. Forks the ladder; needs Pip's content. Also: the onboarding -> scouting HANDOFF (cold-open's final beat should hand an active scouting choice, not end on narrative).

2. **The '#789 hire = agile epic' redesign.** Commit/defer all predictable sub-parts of a plan at LAUNCH (agile epic model); a re-entrant plan phase (re-add to the stack as sub-actions resolve, spending reserve from the 20-pool); kill the vestigial legacy 3/turn AP pool (#613 L2 effort economy -- the keystone); laptop auto-provision-from-office-stock (office economy #791/#804). Pin the **nudge / prompt / demand** player-ping vocabulary (maps to event_tiers ambient<feed<window).

3. **Cat doom-oracle (DQ-22 rivals).** Design the cat as a higher-resolution doom instrument (on-thesis: earn resolution, no printed deltas). HOLD the rival-steal stacking-modifier for now (Pip's T6 ruling) -- oracle first.

4. **Cadence + two-league ratification (quick).** Ratify docs/RELEASE_AND_LEAGUE_CYCLE.html: the two-cadence model (weekly seed / monthly epoch) + the **two-league** idea (stable main league + a discoverable opt-in experimental/balance league that can churn). Verified sound: a new seed correctly gets its own board on the same epoch, no fork.

Standing/known (finish-or-drop, do NOT stack): doom-floor decline-bound N; founding-weight vs fast-replay; the save-scum / Orb-of-Regret leaderboard-integrity fork.

## Prep before WS-3
- Finish the ADR-0015 data strip (remove the 40 inert doom-delta fields) -- latent landmine.
- Land the Attention-aware balance sweep (in flight) so #789/#803 pacing can be validated.
- The metabolic-cycle reflective review is a SEPARATE later gate (#808, on/after 2026-08-24).

Pip: the three days run per the runsheet -- Mon workshop-around-chunks, Tue drive-by approvals only, Wed full workshop day, hard stops throughout. Send your CEO-chunk times when known and the MOVABLE placeholders get pinned; flag any clash and I will reshuffle + update the calendar.

issues.title: data: morning-briefing metric stubs -- passive, append-only collection architecture
issues.body:
Pip vision 2026-07-26 (future life-orchestrator prints a paper morning briefing; no-screen mornings; the attention trap is RESPONDING, so the medium is inert paper). pdoom1's job NOW: gently architect the collection stubs so the briefing can exist later.

Design principles: passive append-only timestamped snapshots (the verdict-log pattern); low cardinality; nothing new to operate daily; aggregation lives with the website repo's existing snapshot schedulers / pdoom-data, pdoom1 just ensures everything is API-derivable or emitted.

| Metric | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Release downloads by platform | GitHub releases API (per-asset download_count) | EXISTS -- needs daily snapshot row |
| Issues opened/closed by label+criticality | GitHub API | EXISTS -- snapshot row |
| Leaderboard submissions + distinct players | remote board (PHP) / leaderboard files | EXISTS -- snapshot row |
| Website uniques/pageviews | website repo analytics snapshots (already scheduled) | EXISTS |
| Bug reports (F8 -> email) | manual count for now | STUB: count lands in ping later |
| Install base / active-ish players | #799 anonymous ping (one request, two jobs) | THE new stub -- build with a counter endpoint |
| **Inferred people-hours** (Pip's triumph metric) | leaderboard turns-survived x est. minutes/turn; later ping session aggregates (privacy-respecting per user_privacy.json posture) | STUB: define the formula now, refine inputs later |
| Social/Manifund aggregates | manual/API later | DEFER |

Gentle-now action: one daily_metrics.json schema + a scheduled snapshot appender (website repo or pdoom-data owns it -- cross-repo call via Pip per protocol); pdoom1 side = #799 ping + the people-hours formula documented. The briefing renderer itself belongs to the future orchestrator repo, not here.
